seo.meta_title: 해냈어! | Korean -아/어 내다 for Getting Through Something Hard
seo.meta_description: AI translates 'I did it!' as 내가 했어! Koreans say 해냈어! Learn -아/어 내다: 이겨 내다, 버텨 내다 — common in K-pop lyrics and speeches.

ai_failure.situation: You passed TOPIK level 4 after two tries and want to text your Korean teacher 'I did it!'
ai_failure.ai_mistake: Writes 내가 했어! or 제가 했어요!, which sounds like 'I was the one who did it.'
ai_failure.why_it_fails: 했어 just states who did it. 내다 after a verb adds 'all the way through, despite difficulty'. 해냈어요 is the triumphant 'I did it!' Koreans actually say.

natural_solution.rule: Verb + 아/어 내다 = pull through, achieve against the odds. Use it when effort and difficulty are the point.

alternatives.context: 'You got through a hard time' — praise or comfort
'I found out the cause' — figured out after digging

nuance: 내다 ('put out, produce') turns effort into a result. It's everywhere in encouragement: 이겨 낼 수 있어 ('You can overcome this'), 견뎌 내다 ('endure'). That's why it's a favorite in K-pop lyrics, award speeches and comfort messages. Without 내다, the same sentences sound flat.
